body: In principle I think not firing events for the `iframe` element removal case is reasonable as the primary purpose for these events is navigation and history traversal.

I ran an HTTP Archive and live-page compatibility study in Chromium (`--enable-blink-features=OmitSubframeDetachmentEventsOnRemoval`) to check whether we can stop firing `pagehide`, `visibilitychange`, and `unload` synchronously on `<iframe>`/`<object>` DOM removal altogether (matching the HTML Standard), or whether we need a compromise gated on ancestor DOM script access to avoid synchronous re-entrancy. Across 367 assessable live mobile pages (281 stratified random + 86 CrUX top-1,000), we found **0 visual or user-facing regressions** under either approach: omitting the events for all subframes suppresses only analytics beacons or benign cleanup on ~186,528 (1.21%) mobile root pages, while gating on script access to any ancestor (`canAccessAnyAncestor`) eliminates synchronous ancestor DOM re-entrancy while touching ~3,937 (0.026%) pages.

AI summary of the research ([gist](https://gist.github.com/noamr/f80676a616444de7efb5be671692e919)):

> In the `2026-10-01` HTTP Archive mobile crawl (`15,366,242` root pages), `PageHideFired` or `DocumentUnloadFired` fired on `474,165` pages (`3.086%`, including `57` CrUX top-1,000 pages). We compared default Chrome `156` against `--enable-blink-features=OmitSubframeDetachmentEventsOnRemoval` with an all-frames DOM-removal and listener tracer (verified against a 6-case local suite covering direct, ancestor/React container, `innerHTML`, `<object>`, cross-origin OOPIF, and `A1 -> B -> A2` sandwich removals) across `320` stratified random mobile pages and `100` CrUX top-1,000 mobile pages.
>
> | Comparison (`474,165` `fired` mobile pages) | Broken / User-facing | Benign cleanup | Invisible telemetry | Unaffected | Not assessable |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | Visual diff (all subframes) | ~0 (0–18,181) | — | — | ~410,248 | ~63,917 |
> | Runtime listeners: all subframes (HTML Standard) | ~0 (0–18,181) | ~43,305 | ~143,223 | ~223,721 | ~63,917 |
> | Runtime listeners: `canAccessAnyAncestor` compromise | ~0 (0–18,181) | ~3,937 | ~0 | ~406,312 | ~63,917 |
>
> Zero pages were rated `broken`, `worse`, `improved`, or `user-facing` in either sample (including `0 / 47` assessable CrUX top-1,000 `fired` pages). Note that a compromise gated only on immediate `parent` access misses `A1 -> B -> A2` cross-origin sandwiches where `A2` still detaches synchronously during `A1`'s DOM mutation; see the [full report](https://gist.github.com/noamr/f80676a616444de7efb5be671692e919#file-00-readme-md) for option details, script-group verdicts, and reproduction scripts.
